headline: Nasdaq vol printed a seven-month low into Warsh's first keynote at 10am, and PayPal's $53bn bid died overnight.
stance: PYPL -12% overnight (~6am ET). The setup is the risk, not the speech: VXN closed at its lowest since January, month-end rebalancing lands in the same hour as the podium, and nothing this week gave anyone a reason to hedge.

news.head: Advent and Stripe walked away from PayPal
news.body: The consortium dropped its $60.50-a-share, $53bn approach on regulatory and financing concerns after the board called the price insufficient.

news.head: The 7-year left dealers more than the 5-year did
news.body: $44bn cleared at 4.512% with 2.50x cover, better than Wednesday. Dealers were left 12.3% of the competitive award against 10.0% at five years.

news.head: Claims printed 203k
news.body: Consensus was 206k and the four-week average sits at 206k. The series September now turns on did not crack in the week before the keynote.

news.head: Warsh takes the podium at 10am ET
news.body: First symposium address as chair, 19 days before the September decision. Michigan final sentiment prints in the same minute.

implications: A debut keynote is a framing exercise, not a policy move. With core at 3.3% and July payrolls negative, whichever half of the mandate he names first is the September trade.
The PayPal break pulls the sponsor bid out of a group that has carried an option premium since July. It re-rates every large fintech the market assumed was takeable.

watch.head: Warsh, 10am ET
watch.body: Rate vol was sold every session of this week into an event nobody can position for twice. There is no cushion left in the price if he ranks the mandate.

watch.head: Michigan final, 10am ET
watch.body: Consensus 51.0 against 55.2 prior, with one-year inflation expectations seen at 4.3% from 4.2%. It lands in the same minute the podium goes live.

watch.head: Month end, last business day
watch.body: A rebalance and a Fed chair's first framing share one tape. Treat the opening hour's flow as mechanical until it proves it is not.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: $183bn of coupons cleared and claims came in under consensus. The week ended with nothing left to hide behind: the next repricing of September comes out of a microphone.
Dealers were left 12.3% at seven years against 10.0% at five, and cover still improved. The bid did not vanish, it stopped paying up past the belly.
sections.positioning: Spec net long 5-year Treasury sits at the 93rd %ile of three years alongside the 2-year at the 100th. The whole duration lean is parked where this week's supply hit hardest.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: VXN closed at 20.24, its lowest since January, the session after the largest single-name event of the quarter. Vol got sold into the gap, not bought ahead of the podium.
The index gained while its average member lost ground: S&P names above their 50-day line fell to 55.8% from 59.6%. Thursday's move was carried, not shared.
sections.positioning: Spec net long S&P 500 fell five percentiles on the week to the 86th of three years. Someone trimmed the index leg before the keynote; nobody trimmed the vol.

single_name.note: Pfizer - new to the screen today, insider buy filed Aug 12, above its 200-day. At 3.5 days to cover it is real short interest for a name this size.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Tuesday's funding widening did not survive the week. It arrived before the coupon settlements rather than after them, which makes it calendar noise, not balance-sheet strain.
Reserves are at their lowest since April and the RRP has nothing left in it. The last day of August is where that gets tested, not the first week of September.
Equity-credit correlation fell to 0.658, the lowest since March. Credit is trading its own book into month end and no longer taking its cue from the index.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer high-yield inventory rose eight percentiles on the week to the 12th of three years, the largest weekly move in the credit block and still off a very light base.

single_name.note: NGL Energy Partners - two insiders filed buys Aug 26, above its 200-day. At 12.4 days to cover it carries the heaviest short interest on the screen.

ideas.line: 4 open · 0 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
